There is a complete absence of contrast enhancement (ET Volume (mL) is 0.0) and necrosis (NCR Volume (mL) is 0.0). These are the primary imaging hallmarks used to distinguish lower-grade from high-grade gliomas. Without any features of anaplasia such as enhancement, a WHO grade 2 is the most probable diagnosis. overall_comment: The patient is a young adult with a small, solitary, non-enhancing lesion in the right insula and frontal cortex. The young age and lack of any high-grade imaging features (enhancement, necrosis) make an IDH-mutant, WHO grade 2 glioma highly likely. The 1p/19q status is less certain; however, the absence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch sign and relatively sharp tumor borders favor a 1p/19q-codeleted status (oligodendroglioma) over a non-codeleted status (astrocytoma).
